tasks.description: Create a `Todo` dataclass with: `id: int`, `title: str`, `done: bool = False`, `created_at: str`. The created_at should default to today's date string.
tasks.hint:
`from dataclasses import dataclass, field; from datetime import date`
`created_at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(date.today()))`
Using `default_factory` with a lambda lets you compute the default at creation time.
tasks.solution:
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date

@dataclass
class Todo:
    id: int
    title: str
    done: bool = False
    created_at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(date.today()))

t = Todo(1, 'Buy milk')
print(t)
print(t.created_at)
tasks.walkthrough:
The first two fields have no defaults. `done` defaults to False.
`created_at` uses `default_factory` with a lambda so the date is looked up each time a Todo is made, not once when the class is defined.

tasks.description: Create a `TodoList` class: add, complete, delete, and list todos. Assign auto-incrementing IDs.
tasks.hint:
`self.todos = []; self._next_id = 1`
`add(title)`: create Todo with current `_next_id`, append, increment ID.
`complete(id)`: find by id, set `done = True`.
`delete(id)`: filter it out of the list.
tasks.walkthrough:
`add` builds a Todo with the current next id and then increments it, so ids are unique and increasing.
`complete` uses `find` to locate the item and flips its flag. `delete` rebuilds the list without the matching id.

tasks.description: Add `save(filename)` and `load(filename)` methods using JSON. The todo list should persist between runs.
tasks.hint:
`save`: `json.dump([vars(t) for t in self.todos], f, indent=2)`
`load`: `self.todos = [Todo(**d) for d in json.load(f)]`
`vars(t)` converts a dataclass to a dict; `Todo(**d)` unpacks it back.
tasks.walkthrough:
`save` converts each dataclass to a dictionary with `vars()` and writes the list as JSON.
`load` reads it back and rebuilds each Todo with `Todo(**d)`. It then sets `_next_id` past the highest loaded id so new items don't clash.

tasks.description: Build the CLI menu: 1) Add todo, 2) Mark done, 3) Delete, 4) List all, 5) Save & Exit. Show pending count in the menu.
tasks.hint:
Count pending: `pending = sum(1 for t in todos if not t.done)`
Display: `print(f'--- Todo List ({pending} pending) ---')`
Main loop: `while True: show_menu(); choice = input('>'); handle_choice(choice)`
tasks.walkthrough:
The loop shows the menu with the pending count, reads a choice and dispatches to a method.
`ask_id` wraps the int conversion in try/except so typing letters gives a message instead of a crash.
Option 5 saves and breaks out of the loop.

tasks.description: Polish the app: colour-code done todos, add input validation, handle file-not-found on load gracefully, and show creation date.
tasks.hint:
ANSI codes for colour: `'\033[92m'` = green, `'\033[0m'` = reset.
Print done todos in green, pending in white.
For file load: `try: todo_list.load(...) except FileNotFoundError: pass` — start fresh if no file.
tasks.walkthrough:
Loading is wrapped in try/except so the very first run, with no file, starts with an empty list instead of crashing.
Done items are printed in green using ANSI codes, and every item shows its creation date in dim text.
Empty titles are rejected. Everything else is the menu from the previous step.

lesson.intro:
The last project: a to-do list you can use from the terminal, that remembers
its items between runs. It brings together dataclasses, a class that manages a
collection, JSON for saving, a menu loop, and a bit of polish. Build it in the
five steps below and run after each one.

sections.heading: Step 1: the Todo dataclass
sections.body:
Four fields. `created_at` needs a default computed at creation time, so
use `field(default_factory=...)` with a lambda that returns today's date
as a string.
sections.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date

@dataclass
class Todo:
    id: int
    title: str
    done: bool = False
    created_at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(date.today()))

print(Todo(1, 'Buy milk'))

sections.heading: Step 2: the TodoList class
sections.body:
Holds a list of todos and a counter for the next id. `add` creates a
Todo and bumps the counter; `complete` and `delete` find by id. A small
`find` helper avoids repeating the search loop.

sections.heading: Step 3: save and load with JSON
sections.body:
`vars(todo)` turns a dataclass into a dictionary; `Todo(**d)` turns a
dictionary back. After loading, set the next id to one more than the
highest existing id so new items don't collide.
sections.code:
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Todo:
    id: int
    title: str

todos = [Todo(1, 'a'), Todo(2, 'b')]
text = json.dumps([vars(t) for t in todos])
print(text)
print([Todo(**d) for d in json.loads(text)])

sections.heading: Step 4: the menu
sections.body:
Show the options and a pending count, read a choice, branch. Each branch
calls one method on the list. Convert ids with `int()` inside a `try`
so a typo doesn't crash the program.
sections.code:
pending = 2
print(f'--- Todo List ({pending} pending) ---')
print('1) Add  2) Mark done  3) Delete  4) List  5) Save & Exit')
sections.output:
--- Todo List (2 pending) ---
1) Add  2) Mark done  3) Delete  4) List  5) Save & Exit

sections.heading: Step 5: polish
sections.body:
ANSI escape codes colour terminal text: `'\033[92m'` starts green,
`'\033[0m'` resets. Handle a missing save file with
`except FileNotFoundError` so the first run starts fresh. Show the date
each item was created.
sections.code:
GREEN = '\033[92m'
RESET = '\033[0m'
print(f'{GREEN}[x] done item{RESET}')
print('[ ] pending item')

watch_out: `created_at: str = str(date.today())` without `default_factory` is evaluated once when the class is defined, not per todo.
After loading from JSON, reset `_next_id`, or new todos reuse old ids.
`int(input(...))` on an empty or non-numeric answer raises ValueError. Catch it in the menu.
The output panel in this app doesn't render ANSI colours; you'll see the escape codes as text. They work in a real terminal.
